terms.comment: First a leather corselet, then any cuirass, even one of linen (Suet. Galb. 19; Lewis & Short); also a breastwork on a rampart (Caes. BG 5.39). De Vaan lists it among the derivatives of lōrum, a thong, while reporting that some take it for a loan word.
Greek θώραξ, the chest, and so the armour over it; rarer than lōrīca.

terms.gloss: armour, equipment, a kind of arms; levis armātūra, light-armed troops
evidence: Cic. Phil. 10.14: nostrae sunt legiōnēs, nostra levis armātūra (Lewis & Short)

phrases.english: instead of a breastplate I’ll take a soft cloak

phrases.latin: nostrae sunt legiōnēs, nostra levis armātūra
phrases.english: the legions are ours, the light-armed troops are ours

sources: Lewis & Short: lorica · Lewis & Short: thorax
Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), s.v. lōrum.
